en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Tenth Chapter
The Discussion on Non-intimation as Immorality:
Is non-intimation immorality?
Yes, it is.
“Is it killing?
“One should not say so.
…pe… “Is it taking what is not given?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “sexual misconduct”?
It should not be said thus … [as before].
"Is it false speech?
"One should not say so... [as before] ...
"Is it the occasion for negligence through fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants?"
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ...When one who has undertaken an evil deed gives a gift, do both merit and demerit increase?
It should not be said thus... [as before] ...
Is it the case that both merit and demerit increase?
Yes. [Is this so] for two types of contact? ...pe... [and so on].
Is there a convergence of two consciousnesses?
One should not say so …pe… [and so on for] two contacts …pe…
Is there a convergence of two states of consciousness? Yes.
Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterparts—such phenomena—come into manifestation simultaneously?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameable and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterparts, come into manifestation? Yes.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Monks, these four things are extremely remote from one another. Which four?”
“Monks, the sky and the earth—
this is the first pair that are very far apart … [as before] … Therefore, the Dhamma of the virtuous is far from those who are wicked.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes, [they do].
Therefore, it should not be said that “wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright with their counterparts, come into manifestation. …pe…
Is it not to be said that “non-intimation is immorality”?
Yes, it is.
"Was he not one who had undertaken evil karma?
"Yes.
"If indeed he had undertaken evil karma, then, verily, it should be said of him:"
“Non-intimation is immorality.
The discussion on non-intimation as immorality is concluded.
The tenth chapter.
Its summary verse:
When the five aggregates sought for rebirth have not ceased, the five aggregates of functional activity arise;

for one possessing the Path, material form is the Path; for one possessing the fivefold sense-consciousness, there is the cultivation of the Path; the fivefold sense-consciousnesses are both wholesome and unwholesome.
The five types of sensory consciousness involve mental effort; one who possesses the path is endowed with two kinds of virtue;
virtue is not a mental factor; virtue does not follow the mind; virtue increases through the cause of formal undertaking; manifest virtue is non-manifest unvirtuousness.
The Second Fifty.
Its summary verse is:
"The certainty, the inclusion, the benefit, and cessation."
